media_work.title: Drawn to Injustice: The Wrongful Conviction of Timothy Masters
media_work.focus_or_theme: Case study of Timothy Masters, wrongfully convicted based on his violent artwork and writings as a teenager
media_work.key_statistics: Timothy Masters spent nearly 10 years in prison for a crime he did not commit

key_quotes_raw: "It's hard for me to review this one without judging what happened to Timothy Masters. He was accused of a murder he clearly didn't commit and was convicted because a detective didn't want to admit he'd made a mistake?!?!?!" (Goodreads review)
"This is a well-written book about a horrible tragedy and how it ruined one man's life." (Goodreads review)
systemic_issues_raw: Police tunnel vision and confirmation bias
Failure to properly investigate alternative suspects
Misuse of circumstantial evidence (artwork and writings)
Lack of physical evidence connecting Masters to the crime
policy_recommendations_raw: Need for more rigorous standards for forensic psychology testimony
Stronger enforcement of Brady disclosure requirements
More thorough consideration of alternative suspects
additional_resources_raw: DNA testing that eventually exonerated Masters
Colorado Attorney General's official exoneration in 2011
Civil lawsuits against Fort Collins and Larimer County
Documentary about the case (mentioned in research)

research_notes_other.this_book_is_particularly_valuable_for_o:
1. Provides a first-person account from the wrongfully convicted individual himself
2. Highlights how non-scientific evidence (artwork and writings) can be misinterpreted and lead to wrongful convictions
3. Demonstrates the impact of tunnel vision and confirmation bias in investigations
4. Shows how withholding evidence can lead to wrongful convictions
5. Illustrates the power of DNA evidence in exonerating the innocent
The book offers a unique perspective as it is co-authored by the exoneree himself, providing direct insight into the experience of being wrongfully convicted and the psychological impact of such an experience.

media_item.item_title: Book Content: Drawn to Injustice: The Wrongful Conviction of Timothy Masters
media_item.focus_or_theme: Case study of Timothy Masters, wrongfully convicted based on his violent artwork and writings as a teenager
media_item.summary_notes: This book provides a first-person account of Timothy Masters' wrongful conviction, highlighting the misinterpretation of his artwork and writings, police tunnel vision, withheld evidence, and the eventual exoneration through DNA evidence. It offers insights into the psychological impact of wrongful conviction.
media_item.case_details_raw: Timothy Masters was wrongfully convicted in 1999 for the 1987 murder of Peggy Hettrick in Fort Collins, Colorado.  His conviction was based on the interpretation of his teenage artwork and writings by forensic psychologist Dr. J. Reid Meloy.  Police tunnel vision, particularly by Detective Jim Broderick, and prosecutorial misconduct in withholding evidence contributed to his conviction.  He spent nearly 10 years in prison before being exonerated in 2008 (officially 2011). He received settlements from Fort Collins ($5.9 million) and Larimer County.

contributing_factors_raw: Flawed forensic psychology (Dr. J. Reid Meloy analyzed Masters' teenage drawings and concluded they represented him reliving the crime)
Police tunnel vision (Detective Jim Broderick focused on Masters early in the investigation)
Misinterpretation of evidence (Masters' violent artwork and writings as a teenager)
Failure to consider alternative suspects (including Dr. Richard Hammond)
featured_individuals.status_raw: Exonerated, received settlements from Fort Collins ($5.9 million) and Larimer County
organizations_involved_raw: Special prosecutors assigned to the appeal
Defense attorneys who arranged for touch DNA testing
